head: e9e35067fc3b419a54d790a71663071455f203f1
changes: ProgramBuilder::finish moves source operations out and drops construction interning/folding caches before allocating packed rows and reference arrays.
A metadata-only pass counts ALU, cubic and hash rows, checks height, and allocates row storage at final sizes.
Full and partial row vectors request exact remaining lane counts; original interleaved flush order, hint routing and partial ALU-before-cubic order are preserved.
The conservative worker assignment, proof parameters, wire encoding, registry identities and activation are unchanged.

validation.initial_build_failure: The new invalid-source tests initially called bit instead of bit_hint. The test API calls were corrected before the successful second build; both build logs are preserved.

limitations: Construction map growth and reallocations before finish still require a bounded lifetime model; this does not establish a complete host profile.
Qualification retains the same 3 GiB worker/4 GiB aggregate host and 7 GiB managed GPU/1 GiB allocation caps. No scheduler reservation was reduced based on measurement.
The observed host peak reduction is for this matched full-size fixture, not a general host bound or throughput claim.
Adaptive GPU phases still need aggregate-cap reservations unless a runtime tile constraint is introduced; ordinary fleet planning still rejects the phase-less qualification profile.
Both finalizers prove the same terminal statement through distinct verified dependencies. Their timings are not sustained transactions per hour.
Other transaction types, nonempty-child full-size merges, larger blocks, sustained pool throughput, multi-GPU saturation and AMD/Metal qualification remain open.
